summary: Cross-file constancy analysis of the six Revit 2026 samples resolved all four slice questions and, in doing so, cracked the real reason the corpus's gzip data appeared to have corrupt trailers: every Revit stream is stored page-framed — 64,896 (0xFD80) logical bytes followed by a 353-byte per-page trailer block (stride 65,249) — and the previous extraction inflated the framed bytes. After removing the frames, every deflate stream in every file is stock zlib gzip with a VALID CRC32+ISIZE trailer; the true schema (Formats/Latest) is 496,597 bytes (identical in all 6 files and in a 2026 .rfa), not the 498,766-byte artifact currently in extracted/. Deliverables: tools_cross/compare.py (reproducible report + deframe()/inflate_member() helpers), docs/streams/07-cross-file.md (spec section), plus a critical alert in docs/inbox/cross-file.md.
key_findings: PAGE FRAMING (certain): raw OLE stream = pages of 64,896 payload bytes each followed by a 353-byte trailer block at raw offsets 64896+n*65249. Proven by a unique-solution splice search (removing 353 bytes at 64896 and 130145 makes racbasic Formats/Latest inflate to exactly ISIZE 496,597 with matching CRC32 0x26852216), by the same frame offsets fixing an independently-compressed copy of the same schema in a 2026 .rfa, and by CRC/ISIZE validation of every stream in all 6 files after de-framing (incl. 109-frame dach ContentDocuments and 196/196 sampled members across 129 MB / 1,978 frames of dach Partitions/84). The block is physically contiguous inside the CFB stream, so it is Revit's writer, not an OLE artifact.

GZIP TRAILERS ARE VALID (contradicts KNOWLEDGE.md): after de-framing, the 8 bytes after every deflate payload are a correct CRC32 LE + ISIZE LE; the deflate is textbook zlib (dynamic blocks, one 00 00 ff ff sync-flush, then 02 0c 00 Z_FINISH). The 'corrupt/absent trailer' and the '270-712 undecoded trailing bytes' were framing artifacts. Trailing layout: gzip trailer(8) + zero pad(0-497) + final partial-page trailer block (~353*lastPageLen/65249 bytes for large streams, floor ~37-91 for small).

CORPUS INTEGRITY: extracted/*.gz/*.bin from tools/scan_gzip.py is silently corrupt beyond the first frame for every stream/member whose compressed extent crosses raw offset 64896: Formats/Latest schema wrong from payload offset 138,858 (true size 496,597, sha256 6459a9a93ebde32c26e4190de2756bf7a4592e63a0d142feca43c392ecdf8ac2), racbasic Global/Latest true size 1,500,644 (not 1,506,910), 90/400 sampled Partitions/15 members fail CRC as extracted (89/90 verify after de-framing), and the four previously-undecodable streams (dach ContentDocuments/ElemTable, racadv ContentDocuments, rme ElemTable) decode perfectly after de-framing.

8-BYTE Global/* PREFIX (resolved): a per-stream-name constant identical in all 6 files - Latest=5, ContentDocuments=1, DocumentIncrementTable=1, History=1, ElemTable=0, PartitionTable=0 (u64 LE); Partitions/<N> begins with u64 9. Not a size/count/offset. [hypothesis] per-object serialization version/flags word (ADocument=5, its externalized members 0/1).

CONTENTS WRAPPER (magic 62 19 22 05 = 0x05221962): [0]magic [4]u32 0x1c=28 [8]u32 1 (item count) [12]u32 0 [16]magic again [20]u32 varies per file (183/430/213/424/264/178, meaning open) [24]gzip member with valid trailer, then zero pad + ~42-byte final page block. RevitPreview4.0 uses the same wrapper with item word 0x0000800C = flag 0x8000 (uncompressed) | class 12 (A3PartyAImage, matching its FilePreview m_pAImage) - so the low word is likely a type/class-id word.

IDENTITY: Formats/Latest inflated payload identical across all 6 files and the .rfa (496,597 bytes); Global/PartitionTable (87-139 B) and Contents (240-274 B) inflated payloads are 6 distinct per-file records with a constant skeleton (PartitionTable const header 800c0100000001000000 + GUID shared by 4 files; Contents contains build string 20250227_1515, GLOBAL name, GUID shared with PartitionTable, username in worksharing files).

RAW-HEAD CONSTANCY: Formats/Latest 256/256; RevitPreview4.0 254/256 (wrapper + FilePreview schema stub + PNG); TransmissionData 249/256 (u16 length + fixed UTF-16 XML prolog); BasicFileInfo 210/256; ProjectInformation 117/256 (ZIP; all six share the same Autodesk temp-dir path C:\Users\hansonje\...\d53929fb-..., i.e. exported in one session); Global/* only their prefix+gzip header (18-26); Partitions/<N> 46/256 (44-byte header: u64 9, u32 0x3a3 const, first-record length at [28..31] = firstMemberEnd-36).

The 353-byte page-trailer block is deterministic per page content, starts 0x00, ends 0x00/0x01, high entropy, not any standard hash of the page and not Deflate64; final partial page gets a proportionally shorter block. [hypothesis] compressed per-page integrity/ECC record - irrelevant for reading, required to reproduce for a native .rvt writer (open problem).
confidence: high — page framing and gzip-trailer validity are certain (validated by CRC32/ISIZE on every gzip member of every stream in all 6 files after de-framing, an external 2026 .rfa cross-check, and physical-offset contiguity in the CFB); prefix table and Contents wrapper offsets are direct byte facts; the semantics of the prefix, the Contents item word at 0x14 and the 353-byte page-trailer block are labeled hypotheses.
open_questions: What the 353-byte per-page trailer block (and its shorter final-page variant, 37-353 bytes) encodes; whether Revit's reader validates it (a native writer must reproduce it).

Whether the page constants 64,896/353 are universal (older releases, .rfa, worksharing files) - 2016-2025 .rfa schemas show the same too-long-inflate symptom so they are framed, but their constants are unverified.
Meaning of the Contents item word at offset 0x14 (183/430/213/424/264/178): not a size, checksum, ISIZE or per-release class ordinal (schema identical, value differs).
Semantics of the u64 stream prefixes (5/1/1/1/0/0, and 9 on Partitions) beyond 'per-stream constant'.
Rule for the zero-pad length (0-497) between the gzip trailer and the final page block.
next_steps: ORCHESTRATOR: merge docs/inbox/cross-file.md into KNOWLEDGE.md - replace the 'corrupt gzip trailer' and 'undecoded 270-712 trailing bytes' entries with the page-frame + valid-trailer facts; add a de-framing step (drop 353 bytes at raw offsets 64896+n*65249) to tools/scan_gzip.py / src/rvt readers and require CRC32/ISIZE verification of every inflated member.

Re-run the extraction so extracted/*.gz/*.bin are de-framed and CRC-verified, then re-derive the Formats/Latest schema (true 496,597-byte payload) and any class-ordinal tables built from the old 498,766-byte artifact (correct only up to offset 138,857).

Notify the schema/Global-Latest/Partitions agents that their inputs beyond the first ~64.9 KB of compressed data (and any Partitions member crossing a frame) were corrupt and must be re-decoded from de-framed data.

Reverse the 353-byte page-trailer block (compare full-page blocks of an all-zero synthetic page vs real pages; test whether Revit opens a file with a mutated block) - prerequisite for the direct .rvt writer track.
Resolve the Contents item word at 0x14 by correlating it with DocumentIncrementTable / History counters and the RevitPreview class-word convention.
